Grep node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react for `loginIDPUser`, `authorizeIDP`, `idp`, `social`.

2. **What Zimmermann has**: grep the whole repo excluding node_modules for `social`, `idp`, `IDP`, `apple`, `Apple`, `google` (careful: google maps/GTM will be noise — filter to auth-relevant hits). Is `social-login` overridden under overrides/app/components/? Is there any Apple/Google icon in overrides/app/components/icons? List overrides/app/components/icons contents.

3. **The login drawer**: read overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmAuthDrawerContent/index.tsx and overrides/app/hooks/use-auth-modal.tsx. Does the Zimmermann login UI have any slot/space for social buttons? Is it a custom drawer or a wrapped base component?

4. Check .docs/ in repo root for anything about social login / Apple / Google sign-in: grep -ri "social login\|apple id\|sign in with apple\|google sign" .docs/

5. Report the exact config keys needed to enable social login in this codebase, and whether they are set today.

Be precise and factual. Do not speculate. If something does not exist, say so explicitly.

The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

Password reset is supported from the checkout entry page. If reset is initiated from checkout, redirect customer back to checkout to continue; if from My Account, redirect back to My Account (CFD-004).

Saved delivery addresses, billing addresses, and payment methods are pre-populated at the relevant checkout steps for authenticated customers (CFD-005). Active session bag merges with any saved bag on login during checkout, retaining all items (CFD-006). Email address and previously entered delivery details are preserved if the customer exits and returns to checkout (CFD-010).

Marketing opt-in checkbox at checkout entry — unchecked by default on all storefronts **except US (pre-checked)** (CFD-009). Guest opt-ins go to Emarsys via Omneo. Omneo is the system of record for customer identity, loyalty, and clienteling; SFCC syncs bidirectionally via MuleSoft webhooks (CFD-012). Customer authentication uses SFCC Configurable account management; passwords are not migrated from Magento, so all existing customers must reset at go-live (CFD-013).

Checkout entry behaviour is consistent across all domestic storefronts — no market-specific variations in authentication or guest flow (CFD-014).

**Social login (Apple/Google):** Confirmed in scope for launch (overrides original CFD-011, which is now strikethrough). Implementation details still Open — see Open Items.

Two delivery modes; steps differ. Home Delivery is selected by default (CFD-022):

`overrides/app/routes.tsx:15` imports ONLY the named static export from base:
  `import { routes as _routes } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/routes';`

`overrides/app/routes.tsx` never calls that default export — it builds its own array and calls `configureRoutes` itself. Result: `/social-callback` (config/default.js:109), `/passwordless-login-landing` (config/default.js:97) and `/reset-password-landing` (config/default.js:118) appear to have no React route at all.

- `.claude/registry/routes.md` (generated 2026-09-23 from overrides/app/routes.tsx + inherited base routes) lists none of those three paths.

Coming back from Apple/Google, `/social-callback?code=...` falls through to the `/:segments+` catch-all at overrides/app/routes.tsx (CategoryPath), so `SocialLoginRedirect` never mounts, `loginIDPUser` is never called, and the shopper is never signed in.

3. Regenerate the route registry (`node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs`) so `.claude/registry/routes.md` reflects the change.
4. Add a test that asserts `/social-callback` resolves to the SocialLoginRedirect component when social login is enabled.

# Social Login at Checkout — Evidence Report

## Headline

Zimmermann has **already built and shipped a complete, Figma-branded Apple + Google sign-in stack** (SFCC-742 / SFCC-926 / SFCC-11) — hooks, buttons, icons, theme recipe, tests, stories — and social login is **enabled in config on every tier today**. It is wired into the **wishlist** auth drawer only. It is **not** wired into checkout, and checkout currently falls back to the **base SFCC unstyled** social buttons.

I also found one likely-live defect: the **IDP redirect-back route `/social-callback` appears never to be registered** (chip raised separately).

---

## 1. Base SFCC social login support

### Component inventory (only two files exist)
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/social-login/index.jsx`
- `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/social-login/index.test.jsx` (39 lines)

There is no `social-login/**` subtree beyond these. `app/components/social-icons/` is unrelated — it is the footer's Facebook/Instagram/Twitter/YouTube **marketing** links, not auth.

### Supported IDPs — exactly two
`social-login/index.jsx:26-41` defines `IDP_CONFIG` with exactly **`apple`** and **`google`**. No Facebook, no others. Matching is case-insensitive (`index.jsx:57-60`, `name.toLowerCase()`), and an unknown IDP is logged as an error and filtered out of render (`index.jsx:62-72`, `:93-94`).

Icons ship OOTB: `index.jsx:19` imports `{AppleIcon, GoogleIcon}`, defined at `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/icons/index.jsx:147` and `:172` from `app/assets/svg/apple.svg` and `app/assets/svg/google.svg`.

Button labels are bare — `'Apple'` / `'Google'` (`index.jsx:31, :38`), **not** "Sign in with Apple". Styling is generic Chakra: `variant="outline"`, `borderColor="gray.500"`, `color="blue.600"` (`index.jsx:106-109`).

### Auth mechanism (two-legged OAuth redirect)
**Leg 1 — outbound** (`social-login/index.jsx:50, :74-88`):
```js
const authorizeIDP = useAuthHelper(AuthHelpers.AuthorizeIDP)
setSessionJSONItem('returnToPage', window.location.pathname)
await authorizeIDP.mutateAsync({hint: name, redirectURI})
```
`redirectURI` = `buildRedirectURI(useAppOrigin(), getConfig()?.app?.login?.social?.redirectURI)` (`index.jsx:53-55`).

**Leg 2 — return** (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/social-login-redirect/index.jsx`):
- `:42` `useAuthHelper(AuthHelpers.LoginIDPUser)`
- `:54-71` on mount, reads `searchParams.code`, calls `loginIDPUser.mutateAsync({code, redirectURI, usid?})`
- `:74-94` once `customer.isRegistered`, clears `returnToPage`, calls `mergeBasket` with `createDestinationBasket: true`, then navigates back to `returnToPage` or `/account`

SDK surface confirmed in `node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/hooks/useAuthHelper.d.ts:11,13` (`AuthorizeIDP: "authorizeIDP"`, `LoginIDPUser: "loginIDPUser"`) and `node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/auth/index.d.ts:36,41,446-458`.

### Routes
`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/routes.jsx`:
- `:41` `const SocialLoginRedirect = loadable(() => import('./pages/social-login-redirect'))`
- `:56` `export const routes = [...]` — the **static** array. Contains no social route.
- `:131-166` **default export** — the function that conditionally appends the social route at `:153-157`, gated on `loginConfig?.social?.enabled && loginConfig?.social?.redirectURI`.

### Constants
`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/constants.js:248-252` — the only hit is `LOGIN_TYPES.SOCIAL: 'social'`. No `IDP_*`, `APPLE_*` or `GOOGLE_*` constants exist.

### `_app-config`
`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/_app-config/index.jsx` contains **zero** references to `social`, `idps` or `isSocialEnabled`. Config is read at each consumer, not centrally:
- `app/hooks/use-auth-modal.js:404, :412-413`
- `app/pages/login/index.jsx:62, :69-70`
- `app/pages/checkout/index.jsx:67-69`

all using the identical pattern `const {social = {}} = getConfig().app.login || {}` → `isSocialEnabled: !!social?.enabled`, `idps: social?.idps`.

### Base checkout already has a social slot
The chain is fully wired OOTB:
`checkout/index.jsx:67-69, :203-205` → `partials/contact-info.jsx:58, :247-255` → `partials/login-state.jsx:11, :24, :70`:
```js
{isSocialEnabled && idps && <SocialLogin form={form} idps={idps} />}
```
rendered under a divider + `"Or Login With"` heading (`login-state.jsx:28-33`), alongside a "Secure Link" (passwordless) and "Password" button.

## 2. What Zimmermann already has
